newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Virgin to detail Sun Air bid next week.
newsitem.headline: Virgin to detail Sun Air bid next week.

text.p: Britain's Virgin Group is to detail a bid for South African state-owned airline Sun Air towards the middle of next week, a company spokesman said on Friday.
The deadline for pre-qualification bids for the airline, formerly the carrier for the nominally independent homeland of Bophuthatswana, passed on Thursday.
The Virgin spokesman confirmed the firm's interest in Sun Air and said details would be announced next week.
"We are most certainly making a bid for Sun Air," he said.
The Virgin bid is being made with the Bhekilanga consortium of six black empowerment companies.

Virgin Atlantic Airways already flies six flights a week from London to Johannesburg. The group, headed by flamboyant entrepreneur Richard Branson, has also confirmed it has a long term interest in moving into South Africa's financial services market.

South Africa's Business Report newspaper said on Friday that more than 10 bids for Sun Air had been received by merchant bank BOE NatWest and legal adviser Moseneke & Partners who are handling the sale.
One industry source told Reuters that possibly as many as 70 bids had been put in, but the vast majority were unlikely to ever get off the drawing board.
"There will probably be only about half a dozen serious contenders," the source said.
A spokesman for the Department of Public Affairs said he could not comment on the amount of bids received. He added that the process of sorting out the strong candidates had already begun.
"Some are stronger than others," he said.
After the pre-qualification stage stage there are two further phases -- submission of non-binding offers and final offers/completion.
The announcement of which bids will move past the pre-qualification stage will be made next Thursday.
